Emma — thanks, this is straightforward to scope. I sketched a compact benchmarking playbook that fits into your timeline:

Summary (high level)
- Workload slices: 1) Short triage prompt (avg tokens out ~35), 2) Long note summarization (avg tokens out ~420).
- Traffic patterns: steady baseline (30 rps), clinician bursts (sustained 60–120 rps for 30s), microburst spikes (500 rps for 5s).
- Tests: ramp (0 -> target over 15m), soak (30m at target), stress (step to saturation, observe degradation modes).
- Key metrics: TTFT (first-byte from model execution), token latency p50/p95/p99, durable throughput (reqs/s at p95 latency budget), cache-warm vs cold behavior.

Proposed acceptance matrix (draft numbers)
- Short prompt: p95 latency <= 200 ms, p99 <= 450 ms, TTFT (warm-cache) <= 50 ms.
- Long prompt: p95 latency <= 1200 ms, p99 <= 2200 ms, TTFT (warm-cache) <= 120 ms.
- Throughput: sustain 400 reqs/s mixed-slices with p95 under the targets above.
- Concurrency: support 40 concurrent sessions with KV cache enabled, and recover to baseline within 90s after a sustained stress window.

Run plan & deliverables - Day 1: sanity ramp + baseline metrics (ramp/soak)
- Day 2: burst and stress runs + cold-cache characterization
- Deliverable: CSV of runs, percentile tables, replayed trace pass/fail flags, concise executive one-pager with recommended mitigations if any.

I attached a fillable MAP_workload_definition template (XLSX) — please drop in the production samples and confirm the two representative routes we should gate on. Once you confirm routes, we'll schedule runs and share a Kickoff + Run calendar invite.

Questions for you (quick)
1) Which route will be the recruitment flow (short prompt) vs the full-summary flow (long prompt)?
2) Do you need HIPAA evidence artifacts included in the MAP (audit logs, retention config)?

I put a tentative run window of Jun 15–16. If that works I’ll lock resources.

Best,
Priyom Das

Adding a few engineering notes for the acceptance criteria and the MAP wording so the CS and procurement teams have unambiguous gates.

Concrete SLO tweaks (suggested)
- Define TTFT precisely: time from request arrival at Redwood API gateway to first generated token emitted to the client (measured client-side and server-side). Record both."server-TTFT" and "client-TTFT" for transparency.
- Warm-cache vs cold-cache: Warm-cache = first request after prefix KV is primed; Cold-cache = node restart / cold worker. Cold-cache TTFT target should be listed as an informational metric (no-blocker) but recorded for repro.
- Tail-latency gating: require p95 AND p99 targets for each route. If p99 exceeds target but p95 meets target, classify as "conditionally pass" and require mitigation plan (e.g., sharding, smaller response window, model variant fallback).
- Batching policy: include the batching window used during runs; acceptance requires the same batching policy to be enabled in production for the pilot.

Operational run checklist
- Start-of-run: confirm KMS keys, logging retention set to 90 days, and tracing enabled.
- End-of-run: export tokens-per-request histograms, kernel selection logs, and a sample of KV cache hit rates.

I also propose adding a short stress scenario: randomized microbursts (Poisson) to exercise queueing; useful to evaluate tail-latency amplification.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: EdgeHealth MAP — final benchmarking sweep schedule + acceptance matrix (v1)

Emma / team — attached is the consolidated MAP section for performance validation (EdgeHealth_MAP_draft_v1.docx) and the run outputs we captured during the Jun 15–16 sweep (20270614_latency_runs.zip). Below is the executive acceptance matrix and the concrete run schedule we used.

Executive acceptance matrix (v1) — PASS rules: all required rows must be boolean PASS, and any CONDITIONALLY PASS items require a documented remediation plan with owner and ETA.
- Route: /api/v1/triage (short)
  - TTFT warm-cache p95 <= 180 ms: PASS (measured 160 ms)
  - TTFT warm-cache p99 <= 420 ms: PASS (measured 395 ms)
  - p95 latency <= 180 ms: PASS
  - p99 latency <= 420 ms: PASS
  - Throughput sustain (mixed) >= 300 reqs/s: PASS (measured 340 reqs/s)

- Route: /api/v1/note/summarize (long)
  - TTFT warm-cache p95 <= 110 ms: CONDITIONALLY PASS (measured 140 ms; mitigation: enable per-route smaller batch window, owner: Jonas, ETA: 2027-06-23)
  - TTFT cold-cache: informational, measured 780 ms (documented)
  - p95 latency <= 1200 ms: PASS (measured 1,030 ms)
  - p99 latency <= 2200 ms: PASS (measured 1,980 ms)
  - Throughput sustain (mixed) >= 350 reqs/s: CONDITIONALLY PASS (measured 330 reqs/s; root cause: transient queueing under Poisson microbursts)

Notes on runs performed
- Jun 15 02:00–05:00 UTC: Baseline ramp and 30m soak (mixed traffic).
- Jun 15 08:00–10:00 UTC: Sustained microburst experiments (60–120 rps bursts; 5s microbursts at 500 rps sampled).
- Jun 16 01:00–02:30 UTC: Stress to saturation (step to max lanes), captured kernel selection logs and KV hit rates.

Artifacts delivered
- Per-run CSVs with p50/p95/p99, TTFT server/client, tokens-per-request histograms.
- Kernel selection log excerpts and KV cache hit-rate summary.
- One-pager with acceptance matrix and recommended mitigations.

Next steps & timeline
- Jonas to deliver mitigation plan for batching window adjustment (ETA Jun 23) and a follow-up targeted burst run (owner: Jonas).
- Redwood to update MAP one-pager with procurement "close checklist" (owner: Priyom) and route the finalized doc for PO approval.
- Target: PO sign-off by Jun 28 to keep the July 2 pilot close.

If procurement needs explicit language for SLAs or rollback (we do have a short rollback play in the doc), tell me and I’ll expand it into a concise bullet for PO.

Thanks — attaching the files now.

Best,
